Our Strengths Why Swiggy Wins

Our Strengths Why Swiggy Wins
Innovation-Driven Culture
Swiggy’s advantage lies in how many things come together at once. A trusted brand. A scaled technology backbone. A wide partner network. Deep consumer understanding. Strong execution. Together, these strengths help us spot emerging needs early, build for them quickly and scale them across India with speed and discipline.
We keep asking what can be made faster, simpler or more useful. This mindset powers new offerings, sharper propositions and constant experimentation that help us stay close to evolving consumer needs.
Preferred Platform for Partners

Serving Many Missions
Growing and Highly Engaged User Base

Chairman’s Message Building for India’s Next Consumption Era

Chairman’s Message Building for India’s Next Consumption Era
This backdrop is significant for Swiggy. Your Company operates at the intersection of consumption, technology and logistics. As India’s digital economy expands, consumers are becoming more comfortable with app-led commerce, and convenience is moving from being a premium proposition to an everyday expectation. India’s retail market remains digitally underpenetrated. Quick commerce is still early in its evolution. Food delivery continues to have meaningful headroom as more consumers and meal occasions move online. Dining out, events, household essentials, personal care and other everyday needs are all being reshaped by digital access, reliable fulfilment and wider choice.
Governance remains a key priority for the Board. The transition to public markets has strengthened Swiggy’s commitment to transparency, disclosure quality, independent oversight and stakeholder engagement. Our aim is to build a company that not only meets the expectations of a listed enterprise, but earns confidence consistently as an institution operating at the centre of India’s evolving digital consumption economy.

The Board recognises that leadership in fast-growing sectors requires staying power, financial prudence, robust governance and consumer confidence. This philosophy guided our approach to capital deployment. During the year, Swiggy strengthened its balance sheet through the successful Qualified Institutional Placement of INR 10,000 Crores. Along with the monetisation of the Rapido investment, this timely infusion gives your Company the strategic flexibility to invest for the future, navigate competitive intensity and pursue long-term value creation with confidence.
Dear Shareholders,
It gives me great pleasure to write to you at an important stage in Swiggy’s journey. FY 2025-26 was our first full year as a listed company. It marked the beginning of a more mature chapter, where scale, ambition and innovation were matched by stronger discipline, greater transparency and a deeper focus on long-term value creation. The progress achieved during the year reaffirms the strength of your Company’s business model and the clarity of its strategy.

As Swiggy enters its next phase, our priorities are clear: prudent capital allocation, continued technology investments, sharper differentiation and steady progress towards profitability. The journey so far has been exciting, but the future offers an even larger canvas. We will use the foundation built over the years, and the lessons learned along the way, to strengthen our businesses, deepen customer understanding, maintain cost discipline and create sustainable value.
Technology and innovation have always been fundamental to Swiggy’s culture. They allow us to solve evolving consumer needs, improve partner experience and make convenience more reliable, accessible and scalable. What gives the Board confidence is not experimentation alone, but the quality of execution, learning and accountability behind it. As Swiggy grows, this balance between ambition and rigour will remain critical.
Swiggy was built for this shift. Over the years, your Company has not merely participated in emerging categories; it has helped create and shape them. From food delivery to quick commerce, from dining out to newer convenience-led services, Swiggy has designed solutions around real, everyday consumer needs. The purpose has remained simple yet powerful: to elevate the quality of life of urban consumers by offering unparalleled convenience.

India entered the year on a strong economic footing. Despite global uncertainty, geopolitical tensions and uneven growth across major economies, the Indian economy continued to show resilience. Growth was supported by domestic consumption, expanding services activity, infrastructure investment, easing inflation and improving real incomes. Household consumption remained central to India’s growth story, with private final consumption expenditure accounting for its highest share of GDP in over a decade.
On behalf of the Board, I thank our shareholders for their continued confidence in Swiggy. I also acknowledge the dedication of the management team and employees, and the trust of our customers, delivery partners, restaurant partners, merchant partners and brand partners, whose collective contribution continues to strengthen the Company’s platform and purpose.

Responsible growth is equally central to the Company’s future. NSE Sustainability Ratings & Analytics has placed the Company in the ‘Leader’ category, reflecting Swiggy’s performance across environment, social and governance parameters. The Company also continues to advance its 2030 Sustainability Goals, anchored in Climate, Community and Conscience. These include commitments such as achieving a 100% EV delivery fleet, transitioning to 100% renewable energy in direct operations, strengthening circular packaging practices, upskilling and engaging 1 million individuals in the value chain, empowering 100,000 women across the ecosystem, improving delivery partner welfare and strengthening governance and data privacy.
During the year, this purpose translated into broad-based progress across the platform. Food Delivery continued to deepen engagement by expanding the range of occasions and consumer needs it serves. Quick Commerce scaled in a large and competitive market, while strengthening its proposition as a broader everyday convenience platform. Out-of-Home Consumption delivered its first full year of profitability, showing how adjacent businesses can become meaningful contributors when integrated well. Across the platform, increasing cross-pollination continued to reinforce the strength of Swiggy’s integrated ecosystem.

Swiggy’s next chapter will be shaped by the same conviction that has brought us here: to keep building with purpose, serving with care and creating an institution worthy of India’s next consumption era.
Warm regards,
Anand Kripalu Chairperson Swiggy Limited

Out-of-Home Consumption became one of the strongest turnaround stories in the portfolio. GOV grew 50.6% to INR 4,645 Crores, Adjusted Revenue increased 67.3% to INR 412 Crores, and total transactions grew 58.4% to 15.1 million. The business delivered its first full year of profitability, with Adjusted EBITDA of INR 29 Crores and margin of 0.6% of GOV. Average monthly active restaurants grew 30.2% to 46.6k.
During the year, Toing was launched as an affordability-led experiment for budget-conscious consumers through a restaurant marketplace model. Crew was also introduced as part of our effort to explore newer convenience-led services. Not every experiment will scale at the same pace, but each helps us understand where our technology stack, fulfilment capability and consumer relationship can create future opportunities.
Our strategy was not to pursue volume at any cost. We focussed on wallet share, basket quality, availability and operating leverage. Capital Strength and the Ability to Execute
One of the key developments during the year was the strengthening of our balance sheet. We completed an INR 10,000 Crores Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), the second-largest ever in India outside the Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) sector. The issue saw more than 4x demand from domestic and global investors, even amidst market volatility. Looking Ahead

Looking Ahead
The opportunity ahead remains large, and our focus is clear. We will continue to build for more users, more occasions and more purchase missions, while staying disciplined on capital allocation and operating choices. Our integrated platform, reusable technology stack, partner ecosystem and ability to move quickly give us a strong foundation to keep expanding the meaning of convenience for India’s urban consumers.
We also took a more deliberate approach to network expansion. After front-loading investments in dark stores, our focus shifted towards sweating existing assets, improving utilisation and adding stores in a calibrated manner for coverage and debottlenecking. By year-end, Instamart had 1,143 active dark stores, up from 1,021, and total active dark store area of 4.8 million sq. ft. The infrastructure built can support significantly higher throughput as utilisation improves, alongside further assortment expansion for the primary addressable market.

In 2022, Dineout was acquired as a high-engagement adjacency to Food Delivery, with the aim of building a stronger wrapper around restaurant experiences and creating additional revenue streams for the ecosystem. That thesis has played out well. Integration with the Swiggy app, cross-sell from Food Delivery, growth in restaurant partners, flagship dining events and increasing advertising monetisation have all contributed to the performance. Company Overview
Swiggy has progressively diversified its offerings beyond food delivery to include Swiggy Instamart, its quick commerce platform for groceries and household essentials, and Swiggy Dineout, which offers restaurant discovery, table reservations and dining-related experiences. The platform partners with hundreds of thousands of restaurants, retail merchants, brand partners and delivery executives across hundreds of cities, with a focus on enabling reliable and convenient hyperlocal commerce experiences.
Out-of-Home Consumption

Out-of-Home Consumption
Swiggy’s Out-of-Home consumption segment has two primary services, Swiggy Dineout and Swiggy Scenes. Dineout offers a platform for users to discover restaurants and make reservations, while Scenes is a dedicated platform for booking in-restaurant events, enhancing the Company’s presence in dining-related services beyond food delivery. The services leverage Swiggy’s consumer base and tech capabilities, cross-pollinating users and brand salience for a stronger relationship with both users and restaurant partners. Dineout was one of the few acquisitions by Swiggy in its journey and was integrated into its unified app a couple of years back. These services strengthen Swiggy’s presence in the lifestyle and dining space, catering to the evolving preferences of urban consumers seeking premium dining and entertainment options.
Swiggy Limited (hereafter referred to as “Swiggy” or “the Company”) is India’s pioneering on-demand convenience platform, transforming the way consumers access food and everyday essentials. Swiggy offers a range of user-friendly services that enable customers to browse, select, order and pay for food, groceries and household essentials, with deliveries fulfilled through its on-demand delivery partner network.

Established in 2013, the Company was founded with a mission to enhance the quality of life for urban consumers by providing seamless access to daily essentials. Over the years, Swiggy has emerged as a leading player in India’s online food delivery market by leveraging robust technology capabilities, an extensive delivery network and a customer-centric operating model.
Backed by leading global and domestic investors, Swiggy continues to focus on innovation, operational efficiency and customer experience across its platform ecosystem. The Company remains focussed on strengthening its position within India’s rapidly evolving digital consumption and hyperlocal delivery landscape.
In FY 2025-26, the Out-of-Home Consumption segment continued to scale and move towards profitability, with GOV increasing by 50.6% YoY to INR 4,645 Crores, while Monthly Active Restaurants increased by 30.2% to approximately 47k.
Supply Chain and Distribution

Supply Chain and Distribution
Swiggy, through its subsidiary Swiggy Networks (Scootsy), provides supply chain and distribution solutions focused on warehousing, fulfilment and retail distribution for brands, wholesalers and retailers. The business offers integrated warehousing services, including inventory management, in-warehouse processing and packaging solutions, alongside distribution capabilities supported by Swiggy’s logistics network. Swiggy Networks (Scootsy) also partners with brands to support retail expansion and improve distribution reach across markets. By leveraging technology-enabled fulfilment and logistics capabilities, the business aims to improve operational efficiency and delivery reliability across the supply chain ecosystem.
Diversified Offerings
Food Delivery
Swiggy’s Food Delivery business remains the cornerstone of its platform ecosystem, offering a comprehensive on-demand food delivery service that connects customers with a wide selection of restaurant partners through its app and website. The overall platform service currently operates across 720+ cities in India and caters to approximately 18.3 million Monthly Transacting Users (MTUs). In addition to order fulfilment, the platform also provides advertising and visibility solutions to restaurant partners, supporting customer discovery and engagement across the network.

In FY 2025-26, the Food Delivery segment delivered steady growth, with Gross Order Value (GOV) increasing by 20.2% year-on-year (YoY) to INR 34,593 Crores, while MTUs increased by 19.2% to 17.5 million.
Platform Innovations
As a technology-led platform, Swiggy continues to build, test and scale new offerings aligned with its focus on convenience-led consumption. These include adjacent businesses as well as emerging platform opportunities across hyperlocal commerce and digital services. Recent initiatives include Toing, an experimental marketplace designed to explore affordable food delivery and expand category penetration among value-conscious consumers. Swiggy also introduced Crew, a concierge-style assistance platform that helps users plan, coordinate and simplify everyday tasks and experiences, extending convenience beyond transactions.
Quick Commerce
Swiggy’s Quick Commerce business, Instamart, focuses on rapid delivery of groceries and household essentials through a dense hyperlocal fulfilment network. Since its launch in 2020, Instamart has expanded its presence to 125+ cities, supported by a network of 1,143 active dark stores across India. Backed by dedicated delivery infrastructure, the platform has reduced delivery timelines to approximately 13 minutes.

Over time, the business has expanded beyond grocery-led use cases to include a wider assortment across non-grocery categories, resulting in larger dark- store formats and broader SKU availability. Instamart has also introduced larger-format dark stores, referred to as “megapods”, spanning approximately 8-10k sq. ft., capable of housing up to 50k SKUs.
In FY 2025-26, the Quick Commerce segment witnessed strong scale-up, with GOV increasing by 94.1% YoY to INR 28,496 Crores and MTUs rising by 73.7% to 12.3 million. Average Order Value (AOV) increased by 34.4% YoY to INR 691, supported by broader assortment availability and increasing consumer adoption. During the year, the Company added 122 stores, resulting in a significant increase in active dark-store area to approximately 4.8 million sq. ft., representing growth of 21.1% YoY.

Regulatory and Compliance Landscape
Swiggy recognises that risk management is integral to the Company’s strategy. We believe our success as an organisation depends on our ability to identify and leverage opportunities while managing the risks that accompany them. The board has constituted a Risk Management Committee responsible for overseeing the Company’s risk management framework, reviewing the Company’s risk profile periodically, and ensuring that adequate processes are in place for the identification, assessment, and mitigation of key risks.
Governance
Governance
Governance

Governance
The strength of the Swiggy brand is central to user acquisition, partner participation and long-term value creation. Commentary or publicity concerning our business model, partner earnings and well-being, technology, privacy, sustainability practices, or financial performance, as well as intellectual property matters, can influence how the brand is perceived and may give rise to remediation costs.
Reliable, secure and scalable technology is fundamental to our operations. System interruptions or capacity constraints could affect availability and the customer experience, while an evolving threat landscape exposes us to cyber incidents such as social engineering, denial-of-service attacks, credential-based attacks, and malware. A significant incident could disrupt services, affect data, and carry financial and reputational risks.

We operate across food delivery, quick commerce and adjacent services in a dynamic regulatory environment. Changes in laws and regulations, or in their interpretation and enforcement — including those relating to our business model, social security of gig workers, food safety and quality standards, data protection, foreign investment and permitted business models, consumer protection, competition and taxation — could increase our cost of compliance, require adjustments to our business practices, or give rise to claims and operational restrictions.
We maintain clear brand and communication guidelines and a dedicated function that monitors public sentiment and responds in a timely and transparent manner. We proactively share the Company’s progress and contributions with stakeholders and communities, while a consumer- insights function engages with stakeholders to inform continuous improvement of our products and services.
Our enterprise risk management framework is embedded within strategic and operational decision-making. Risks are identified at both the Company and individual business levels, assessed on the basis of their potential impact and likelihood, assigned clear ownership, and the effectiveness of mitigation plans is monitored. Governance of risk is organised in line with the Three Lines Model, all of which are under the oversight of the Board and its Committees.

We operate dedicated security teams and defined frameworks, supported by advanced security tooling, regular testing & maintenance, resilience, and business continuity planning. We run bug-bounty programmes and internal initiatives such as hackathons to identify and address vulnerabilities, conduct periodic security assessments, and sustain a strong security culture through ongoing employee awareness and training.
We maintain a compliance framework and monitor regulatory developments on an ongoing basis. Our legal, compliance and secretarial functions, supported by external advisors where appropriate, work to ensure timely alignment with applicable requirements, and regulatory considerations are embedded within our planning and operational decisions.

Our performance is influenced by broader macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions, including movements in inflation, interest rates, and currencies, as well as shifts in consumer sentiment and discretionary spending. Swiggy Limited is India’s pioneering on-demand convenience platform, revolutionising the way consumers access food and essential services. The Company offers a gamut of user-friendly offerings that allow customers to browse, select, order and pay for food, groceries and household essentials, with deliveries made directly to their doorstep through its on-demand delivery partner network. The Company was established in 2013 with a mission to enhance the quality of life for urban consumers by offering seamless access to daily essentials. The Company has become a household name in online food delivery by leveraging robust technology, an extensive delivery partner network and a customer-centric approach. Over the years, the Company has diversified its offerings beyond food to include Swiggy Instamart (quick commerce for groceries and daily essentials) and Swiggy Dineout (restaurant table bookings and dining deals). The platform partners with hundreds of thousands of restaurants, delivery executives and retail partners across hundreds of cities, aiming to make everyday convenience accessible and seamless.

During the financial year 2025-2026, the Company on a consolidated basis, achieved a total revenue of ` 23,053 crore as compared to ` 15,227 crore in the previous financial year and loss before tax (excluding exceptional item) of ` (4,140) crore as compared to loss of ` (3,102) crore in the previous financial year.

8. MATERIAL SUBSIDIARIES
Swiggy’s food delivery segment continues to be its core business and provides a comprehensive ondemand food delivery service, linking customers with a wide variety of restaurant partners through its app and website. Currently, Swiggy’s food delivery service operates in 700+ cities across India, catering to approximately 18 million users. This segment also offers targeted marketing and advertising support to restaurant partners, boosting their visibility on the platform and increasing customer traffic to their outlets. In FY 2025-26, Swiggy’s Food Delivery segment demonstrated robust growth, with Gross Order Value (GOV) increasing by 20.2% year-on-year (YoY) and Monthly Transacting Users (MTUs) rising by 19 % to 17.5 million. This growth was driven by a strategic focus on underserved markets, including the outskirts of major cities and Tier 2 towns. Innovations like Bolt — which has scaled to nearly 700 cities of launch and now fulfils more than one in every ten Swiggy food orders and other initiatives such as Eat Right (health focused), Desk Eats (workplace meals) and Food on Train have been pivotal in attracting new consumers and increasing order frequency within this mature category. The segment also benefited from the cross-pollination of users from Quick Commerce, with nearly 30% of Instamart users new to the Swiggy ecosystem.

Swiggy, through its subsidiary Swiggy Networks (Scootsy), provides supply chain solutions focused on warehousing, fulfillment and distribution for wholesalers and retailers. Swiggy Networks (Scootsy) offers brands comprehensive warehousing services, including in-warehouse processing, packaging and effective inventory management. Its services also cover product distribution directly to customers or retail partners, utilising Swiggy’s logistics expertise to ensure timely and cost-efficient deliveries. Furthermore, Swiggy collaborates with various brands to help expand their retail presence across India. By offering fulfillment and distribution support, Swiggy Networks (Scootsy) enables these brands to reach a broader audience without requiring extensive in-house logistics capabilities.

SECTION A GENERAL DISCLOSURES
Swiggy is one of India’s largest consumer technology platforms, reimagining how the country eats, shops, and lives. From food delivery and quick commerce to out-of-home dining and corporate solutions, our platform connects millions of consumers with a vast network of restaurants, delivery partners, and small businesses every single day powered by technology, anchored in trust, and built for India’s everyday convenience economy.
Our commitment is simple: to build a business that scales responsibly, creates opportunity inclusively, and delivers impact sustainably.
At Swiggy, our ambition has always been to build a business that creates value at scale while doing so responsibly. We believe that sustainable growth is driven not only by innovation and execution, but by choices that strengthen the resilience of our ecosystem and expand opportunity for everyone who participates in it.
impact across our ecosystem. We continued to invest in the well-being and security of delivery partners with over ` 21 crore disbursed as insurance claims in FY 2025- 26, reinforcing our commitment to supporting them. We also strengthened quality and trust across our restaurant ecosystem, while continuing to create more pathways for inclusion and recognition across our partner network.

These outcomes reflect a broader belief that responsibility cannot sit at the margins of business, it must be embedded into how we build, grow, and serve.
Over the past year, we continued to advance this commitment across key dimensions of environmental stewardship, inclusion, and responsible business conduct.
Our progress has also been recognised externally. During the year, Swiggy achieved a prestigious ‘AA’ rating in the 2025 MSCI ESG Ratings Assessment, reflecting the strength of our sustainability and governance practices. We were also recognised as a ‘Leader’ in the NSE Sustainability Ratings and Analytics with a score of 78, underscoring our performance across environmental, social, and governance dimensions.

As we work towards enabling a more sustainable future, we have accelerated progress on reducing our environmental footprint across both our operations and ecosystem. Our electrification efforts helped avoid 13,308 tonnes of CO2 emissions in FY 2025-26, while initiatives such as Eco-Saver feature successfully optimised delivery routes, resulting in a significant reduction of 8.9 million kilometers traveled in FY 2025- 26, this prevented 812.6 metric tons of CO2 emissions from entering the atmosphere, equivalent to powering 158 average homes with clean energy for an entire year. Through cloud optimisation and infrastructure efficiencies, we also avoided approximately 1,300 metric tonnes of CO2 emissions during FY 2025-26. In parallel, we continued to advance more responsible consumption and circularity, with 3,328 metric tonnes of plastic offset through recycling initiatives.
While we are encouraged by the progress we have made, we recognise that the journey ahead calls for continued ambition and accountability. We remain committed to creating long-term value while contributing to a more inclusive, resilient, and sustainable future.

a. Impairment of investments
Impairment exists when the carrying value of an asset or cash generating unit (“CGU”) exceeds its recoverable amount, which is the higher of its fair value less costs of disposal and its value in use. At the commencement date of the lease, the Group recognizes lease liabilities measured at the present value of lease payments to be made over the lease term. Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements

Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements
6. A Company’s internal financial controls with reference to financial statements is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A Company’s internal financial controls with reference to financial statements include those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the Company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the Company are being made only in accordance with authorisations of management and directors of the Company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorised acquisition, use, or disposition of the Company’s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.

Income tax expense comprises current tax expense and the net change in the deferred tax asset or liability during the year. A contingent liability is a possible obligation that arises from past events whose existence will be confirmed by the occurrence or non-occurrence of one or more uncertain future events beyond the control of the Company or a present obligation that is not recognized because it is not probable that an outflow of resources will be required to settle the obligation. A contingent liability also arises in extremely rare cases where there is a liability that cannot be recognized because it cannot be measured reliably. The Company does not recognize a contingent liability but discloses its existence in the standalone financial statements.

38 Financial risk management
The Company has constituted a Risk Management Committee. The Company has in place a risk management framework to identify, evaluate business risks and challenges across the Company both at corporate level and also separately for each business division. The Company is exposed to various financial risks majorly Credit risk, Liquidity risk, Market risk and Equity price risk. The Company’s senior management oversees the management of these risks with an objective to minimise the impact of these risks based on charters and (in) formal policies.

Similarly, counterparties of the Company’s other receivables carry either negligible or very low credit risk. Further, the Company reviews the creditworthiness of the counterparties on the basis of its financial strength on an ongoing basis and if required, takes necessary mitigation measures.
a. Market risk
Market risk is the risk that the fair value or future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate because of changes in market prices. Such changes in the values of financial instruments may result from changes in the foreign currency exchange rates, interest rates, credit, liquidity and other market changes.
The Company’s maximum exposure to credit risk for the components of the balance sheet is the carrying amounts as illustrated in note 5 and the liquidity table below.
c. Liquidity risk
The Company’s exposure to foreign currency exchange rate risk is very limited, as the Company doesn’t have any significant foreign exchange transactions. Further, the Company’s investments are primarily in fixed rate interest bearing investments. Accordingly, the Company is not significantly exposed to interest rate risk.

Liquidity risk is the risk of being unable to meet the payment obligations resulting from financial liabilities, which may arise from unavailability of funds. The exposure to liquidity risk is closely monitored on company level using daily liquidity reports and regular cash forecast reports to ensure adequate distribution. The Company believes that cash and cash equivalents and current investments are sufficient to meet its current requirements, accordingly, no liquidity risk is perceived.
i. Interest rate risk:
Interest rate risk is the risk that the fair value of future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate due to changes in market interest rates. The Company has no debt obligation during the current year. Therefore, there is no impact of possible change in floating rate on the entity’s profitability.

Moderator: Thank you very much. We will now begin with the question-and-answer session. Your first
question comes from the line of Gaurav Malhotra with Axis Capital.
Gaurav Malhotra: Just a couple of questions on food and quick commerce. So firstly, on food, if you can give us
some sense on what you're seeing in terms of emerging competition from Rapido, we see Flipkart
Minutes also doing something in food. So how are you sort of seeing the landscape?
Sriharsha Majety: Hi Gaurav, Harsha here. I'll take that first question. Actually, as of now, only Rapido is live to
the general public and Flipkart has opened to the public at scale even in Bangalore yet. We are,
of course, closely watching the market. We happen to be participating in this in the value market
through our pilots with Toing.
And we've talked about it extensively in our shareholders’ letter as well. I think over the last 4-
5 quarters, we are closely monitoring the business health, the product market fit. And we're quite
excited by what we are seeing as of now. Competition has begun, but we're able to respond pretty
strongly both from the Swiggy asset platform as well as the Toing asset.
Our sense, however, as of now, and that's the reason why we're investing in Toing also right now
is that we do believe that the market can expand if the right proposition offering value to

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Questions and answers
chunks.text:
is that we do believe that the market can expand if the right proposition offering value to
consumers while being sustainable can be cracked. For us, it's a specific interest also because
Toing in some sense for us insurance of a large profit pool at its worst and in addition to a large
profit pool at its best.
Page 2 of 15
And that is the reason why we continue to play for it. We continue to monitor all the health
metrics and are continuously revising our plans and iterating on the business based on everything
we know.
Gaurav Malhotra: Got it. In the shareholders’ letter, even in food, you have sort of mentioned about investments
towards the affordability trust. So, Toing, is where the affordability focus is. So, is there some
sort of an overlap happening between the food and Toing from an affordability focus
perspective?
Sriharsha Majety: There is some overlap, but we've also talked about the extent of the overlap and how it's been
changing with time. Every passing month as we get scale, we're seeing the overlap actually
improve as in reduce, which is what gives us confidence that it is the opening of a new market.
There is going to be some, but we monitor it closely, and it is a very healthy right now as we
see. And as it scales, it's starting to get better. The overlap percentage is reducing, which for us
increases our confidence that this is the opening of a new market.

chunks.text:
increases our confidence that this is the opening of a new market.

Also, now that you started to sort of refocus on growth, would that also mean that you will be

Nandita Sinha: Nandita here. This quarter, we've got back on the growth trajectory. We've had a good quarter
with a 13.4% QoQ NOV growth. What makes us excited about this growth is the fact that the
quality of growth has been very good. We've seen our retention metrics go up and our frequency
metrics have go up by 4% QoQ. We've added 1.3 million MTUs, as you said.
We've built this on the back of habit building, which has been on the back of cohortized user
bases on which we have done habit building, and we have invested behind our differentiated

chunks.text:
bases on which we have done habit building, and we have invested behind our differentiated
assortment proposition. This makes us confident on the quality of growth that we've been adding.
As a result of this, we believe that as we continue to build the quality of growth, both on the user
side, which is on building our frequency, habits building our differentiated assortment, which
has actually given us great results in terms of the retention that we see on the platform and also
increase the productivity that we have on the throughput of each pod.
This will actually take us towards sustainability and profitable growth. So, this is our journey
that we will continue to make. We are confident of the quality of growth that we've added in this
quarter.
Gaurav Malhotra: Got it. And the second question in terms of the Tier 2 markets and how are you thinking about
it now?
Page 3 of 15
Nandita Sinha: We believe that we have laid out our network in terms of T1 and T2 markets. We will continue
to focus on markets where we are seeing growth in the same manner of building back our
habituated users and reaching out to them through both the habit building categories like fresh
and staples as well as extending our differentiated assortment category.
This is how we will build business and the focus will be to continue to build user quality across
the market as we go forward.

the market as we go forward.

You've mentioned retention cohorts on Instamart at 60% month 1 and so on. So, any colour you

You've mentioned retention cohorts on Instamart at 60% month 1 and so on. So, any colour you

able to also call out that this investment is showing the frequency growth that we are hoping for,

Now you can imagine that in an affordable offering where the average of basket sizes are a
fraction of, say, the main platform it is extremely hard to build the business because it requires
significant density. It requires the cost to serve to match the revenue, which is also a fraction of
the main platform. So our ability to navigate many of this also comes from the fact that we are
building in the back of the original chassis that is fully expressed in the main platform.
So the incremental overhead that we incur is just on user acquisition. The fixed cost is very, very

So the incremental overhead that we incur is just on user acquisition. The fixed cost is very, very

whether this experiment has worked. But enough we see to be able to give you that direction is

metrics look in the right direction. At the same time, we need to continue to scale the business

Swiggy and compare that with Zomato, one gets a sense that for the last couple of quarters, they

looking at it from that point of view.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Questions and answers
chunks.text:
looking at it from that point of view.
Rohit Kapoor: Rohit here. Let me take the question in two parts. On the growth rate, if you see what we’ve
called out in the letter, that in Sep-26 we were back on 20% plus growth just talking about
Swiggy. And we see us maintaining the 18-20% stand-alone guidance on Swiggy. On Toing, 2
out of 3 users that we're seeing are new to platform.
As Rahul mentioned, even on the users who are using both, we are seeing 25% higher orders per
user. It is doing two or three jobs for us clearly the combined strategy. One is open up the market
to a new set of consumers who either have very low frequency on food delivery or they're not
on food delivery.
Point number two is give more choices to consumers on what occasions, which app they want
to use, and they are showing that they are rewarding that strategy with a higher orders per user
frequency. And third, obviously, there's a competitive shift in landscape.

As Harsha said, that clearly, we see there a robust strategy to participate in the market where
there is 10 years of legacy of building a food delivery business and new entrants entering. So it's
insurance we feel, but on the upside, it has significant potential to unlock value in the future.
Sachin Salgaonkar: Clear on that, Rohit. Second question on quick commerce. I see in shareholders' letter, you guys

Sachin Salgaonkar: Clear on that, Rohit. Second question on quick commerce. I see in shareholders' letter, you guys
have mentioned contribution margin to remain in the range of 0 to -100 bps with sequential

of our growth. And the 0 to -100 basis points guidance that we have given was keeping that
flexibility in mind. As you have seen, we have grown at a healthy pace of 13% plus in the

contribution margin from the existing users that we will operate with.

the pace of store expansion. From a coverage standpoint in these cities, we are well covered.

Moderator: Our first question comes from the line of Sachin Salgaonkar with Bank of America. Please go
ahead.
Sachin Salgaonkar: I have three questions. The first question is regarding the strategy in quick commerce. Now
that we achieved a contribution margin breakeven, which partly, perhaps, came at the expense
of a slower growth, management now wants to focus on accelerating growth, but again, that is
going to come at the expense of contribution margin getting again into a negative territory. So I
just wanted to understand how we should think about the strategy? Is it growth at the expense
of margins or vice versa? And when do we see a mix of both?
The second question is on quick commerce on implied take rate. Because when we look at
Quick Commerce NOV growth, it's roughly 3% QoQ, QC revenue growth is roughly 13%.
Clearly, the implied take rate has moved up. So I just wanted to understand, is it on the back of
the mix of private label? Is it seasonality? And how sustainable is the increased take rate?
And the last question is on food. Of late, a lot of noise has been increased on potential
competition in the food delivery space. Would love to hear management's thought on that,
particularly on the zero commission model and how does Swiggy look at it?

Sriharsha Majety: Thanks for your question, Sachin. I'm going to answer the first question, Harsha here.Yes, we
did talk about a plan to be more focused on growth as we think about the way forward. When
we talked about our overall commitment to move to the CM zero, there were a bunch of

reasons that we wanted to do it. We believe that to build a strong foundation for durable
growth, this was quite important, and we have talked about it many times.
When we look at the quality of the business going into the future, we have absolutely moved
close to INR30 in contribution over the last 5 quarters. Our user retention month-on-month is
at the highest that it's ever been. And a lot of the work that we've done on our brilliant basics
as well as our efforts on differentiation are bearing fruit. So at this point where there is outside
of, let's say, the market leaders, there are many folks operating at - 10% and below contribution
margin. That is the kind of segment that we're in.
So in a segment where there are very wide bands of operations that everyone has, we believe
that we have earned the right and the flexibility to operate at a zero to -100 bps contribution
margin level. At the same time, we want to be completely accountable to the quality of growth

Rohit Kapoor: This is Rohit. I'll answer your third question regarding food delivery and the competition
question you asked. So at the base level, we believe that food delivery remains still quite
under-penetrated in India. And with just maybe 1 out of 10 Indians having ever having
transacted on a food delivery platform, and that too a bulk of those transacted probably low
frequency. That's point number one, that the opportunity remains secular and multi-year in
nature.
The second question is, we feel quite good about the kind of robustness we have built on the
Swiggy platform in terms of accelerating growth. So while this quarter growth is coming at
adjusted about 18%, if you adjust for cancellations. But if you've seen the momentum over the
last 3-4 years, it's been on an upward trajectory, and we continue to maintain guidance of YoY
growth between 18% to 20%.
Third, your question on competition, it is quite clear to us that the expansion of food delivery
will happen on the back of affordability and new segments. And also it is very likely that any
competition of any nature which comes in, is likely to come in more in the affordability

competition of any nature which comes in, is likely to come in more in the affordability
segment than the premium segment. The premium segment is much harder to enter for any
new competitor. That's a fair deduction to make.
Now we have made a conscious choice of building on the marketplace model, which is Toing,
but it is very differentiated in terms of the delivery fee charges, the kind of proposition offers,
the cuisine, the last mile, the economics, the value proposition consumer. It looks nothing like
what food delivery looks like in India today. .
There are competitors who are continuing to bet on the micro kitchen model. We believe,
having tried that model and taken a decision to exit it about 4-5 months back, that model a) it
requires a different kind of expertise b) it is probably more expensive to build and c) the
economics of that remain highly uncertain for most players.
Last, your question on zero commission, I think we'll like to walk away from the marketing
element of this to the reality of the business. So while you can call something zero
commission, there are 3-4 fundamental questions to be answered there. One, if it is zero
commission, then who pays for cost of the platform. Somebody has to pay. And in the
medium-term, it is quite clear that there will be some charges, whether they're called
commission or by some other name.

Even today, we believe that while, for example, on Swiggy, we don't charge restaurant partners
for delivery. There are platforms which end up charging for delivery. And if you look at the
lower AOVs and look at those costs, they do not really reflect a zero commission structure.
Secondly, even if it is done initially, it is quite likely that over time as the entry-level response
is done, at some point in time, you'll have to recover the economics, and if it is not going to
come from one stakeholder at all, then it goes to the other stakeholder - to either the consumer
or the delivery partner. We are not sure of the equilibrium that creates or the dissonance it
creates in the future.
So I think given our experience, we believe that the way we architectingToing, it remains one
of the lowest cost ways to bring in a new delivery feature to the market and expand it, and as
we today and in the future, as we expand it, build on it, happy to share more details with
everyone on that. Hope that answers the question.

month back?

escalation in last mile cost in this quarter because of West Bengal elections and hotter than
normal summers. So is it possible to quantify what would have been that impact across both
the food delivery and Instamart?

happens in the Q1FY27 cycle, so that's one part which sits below the contribution margin. Also
we have seen in certain states where there's been a minimum wage hike, which has impacted
certain, say, operations around our picking and packing costs at the warehouse or at the dark
store level. So those have been factored in our current, say, both the achievements in Q1FY27
quarter as well as the guidance that we're giving for the Q2FY27 quarter. So not material, but
something which is already being baked into.
In terms of the last mile cost, you are right. This is a seasonal impact, which got accentuated
